editorial.thesis: A trading-and-learning city of about three million. Its retail is heavy on banks, coaching and apparel, and thin on branded food, café culture and modern grocery — and three in ten residents live in zones with under 60% of the city's average retail depth.
takeaways: Branded retail is early. 5.6 chain outlets per lakh residents against 63 in Bengaluru; 32 of the 51 national brands we track are present, mostly with a handful of stores (Domino's 17, Café Coffee Day 10, DMart 1).

The mapped economy leans to institutions and trade. Education is 13.2% of mapped places (Bengaluru 8.7%), banks and finance 9.9% (6.6%), healthcare 9.5% (7.7%) — while food & drink is 7.9% (10.6%) and daily-needs retail 1.2% (2.5%).

Supply and demand are misaligned. Six zones hold 30% of residents with under 60% of the city's average retail depth. Hamirpur Road–Hanspuram alone has about 267,000 residents and 19 mapped food & drink places.

Retail is concentrated. 44% of commercial places sit in the busiest tenth of the city (Bengaluru 40%). Two cores carry it: Mall Road–Birhana Road (2,032 places) and Ashok Nagar–Kalpi Road (depth index 180).
Value fashion is already organised. V-Mart has as many mapped outlets as Bengaluru's core (10), and Raymond and Bata have 16 each — the formats that work in Kanpur are the ones built for value.

numbers.title: The city in eight numbers
numbers.deck: A 10 km circle around the centre, processed with the same rules as Bengaluru's, so every comparison is like for like. Where raw counts would mislead — because a bigger city is mapped more completely — we compare shares and mix instead.

map.title: Where people live, where shops are
map.deck: Switch layers. The amber “gap” layer is the one to study: it marks places with many residents but little retail around them. Hover any hexagon (about 0.1 km²) for its numbers; click a zone on the right to isolate it.

captions.residents: Where people live. Three zones — Mall Road–Birhana Road, Kidwai Nagar–Yashoda Nagar and Hamirpur Road–Hanspuram — each hold more than a quarter-million residents. Modelled residents per square kilometre.
captions.supply: Where the shops are. Retail is far more clustered than people: the busiest tenth of cells hold 44% of all commercial places, and the Mall Road–Birhana Road zone alone lists 2,032.
captions.chains: Where the brands are. Branded outlets hug the Mall Road core: 45 of the 171 tracked chain outlets sit in that one PIN code, and Swaroop Nagar–Nawabganj adds 21. Most other zones have ten or fewer.
captions.education: Where the campuses are. Kidwai Nagar–Yashoda Nagar (167 education places, 54 of them coaching) and Kakadeo–Geeta Nagar (153, with 79 coaching) are the student belts — a daytime youth market that residents alone do not show.
captions.gap: The gap. Amber: many residents nearby, little retail. Blue: far more retail than local residents explain — the commercial cores that draw people in. The deepest amber sits in Hamirpur Road–Hanspuram and Panki Road–Swaraj Nagar, with large patches in Kidwai Nagar–Yashoda Nagar, Meerpur Cantt and Defence Colony. The blue cores are Mall Road–Birhana Road, Ashok Nagar–Kalpi Road and Swaroop Nagar.

zones.title: Zone by zone, by PIN code
zones.deck: Each zone is a postal-code area. Residents are modelled counts; places are mapped businesses and services. “Retail depth” is places per 10,000 residents — the tick marks the city average. Click a row to see it on the map.

mix.title: What the retail layer is made of
mix.deck: Raw counts per resident would flatter Bengaluru, which is mapped far more completely. So this compares each category's share of all mapped places. 100 means the same share as Bengaluru; below 100 is thinner, above is stronger.
mix.note: Kanpur's mapped places over-index on institutions and trade — education (13.2% of places vs 8.7%), banks and finance (9.9% vs 6.6%), healthcare (9.5% vs 7.7%) — and under-index on modern daily-needs retail (1.2% vs 2.5%), food & drink (7.9% vs 10.6%), offices (10.1% vs 12.7%) and leisure (3.0% vs 3.7%).

chains.title: Who is mapped here, and who is not
chains.deck: 171 outlets of 32 tracked national brands within 10 km — 5.6 per lakh residents against Bengaluru's 63. Filled names have at least one mapped outlet (count shown); dashed names have none.
chains.note: Read dashed names as leads, not verdicts. “No mapped outlet” can mean a brand trades under a different listed name, or has opened since the map was updated. The pattern is still telling: the specialty-coffee and chai chains, organised pharmacy, and modern-trade grocery are where Kanpur is thinnest. Premium reports check every lead against live listings.

formats.title: Which formats have room
formats.deck: Nine formats, thinnest first. The index is the format's share of all mapped places relative to Bengaluru's, so low means thin by Bengaluru's standard. “Where to look” ranks zones with at least 40,000 residents by residents per mapped outlet — a first-pass screen for where one more outlet would face the least local competition.

people.title: Who the customers are
people.deck: Age mix inside the 10 km circle, from Meta's age rasters (modelled, not a census).
people.note: Kanpur has a larger youth share (15–24: 21.7% vs 19.5%) and a slightly smaller working-age share (48.1% vs 50.2%) than Bengaluru's core, with 8.5% aged 60+. Under-25s are over 43% of residents. That fits the education skew in the retail mix, and it favours formats built on frequency and price — fast food, value apparel, coaching-adjacent services — over high-ticket discretionary spend.

zones.208001: The commercial heart: 2,032 mapped places and 45 chain outlets — a quarter of the city's tracked chains — for about 333,000 residents. A destination zone, so much of its footfall likely lives elsewhere.
zones.208012: The densest retail relative to residents (index 180): 992 places for about 144,000 residents. Trade corridors along Kalpi Road and Fazalganj feed it; check for trade-counter activity before reading it as consumer demand.
zones.208011: A student-and-family belt: 167 education places (54 coaching) and 90 healthcare places for about 280,000 residents — but only 76 food & drink places and 10 chain outlets.
zones.208021: The clearest gap in the city: about 267,000 residents, 379 mapped places, 19 food & drink and 2 chain outlets. Depth index 37.
zones.208020: About 143,000 residents with 180 places and a single chain outlet (index 33) — the thinnest large zone in the city.
zones.208025: The coaching hub: 79 coaching centres, the most of any zone, among 153 education places — a youth daytime market for food, stationery and stays.
zones.208002: A healthcare-and-hospitality centre: 159 healthcare places (the most of any zone) and 145 food & drink places for about 193,000 residents.
zones.208006: Compact and well supplied: 475 places for about 79,000 residents (index 156).
zones.208027: About 188,000 residents, education-heavy (118 education places) with 41 food & drink places.
zones.208017: About 177,000 residents and 145 healthcare places — among the highest in the city — against 42 food & drink places.
zones.208022: About 139,000 residents, 316 places and a single chain outlet; 56 education places.
zones.208010: About 127,000 residents and 189 places (index 39), with 2 chain outlets.
zones.208013: About 106,000 residents and 179 places (index 44), with 1 chain outlet.

grocery.read: Modern daily-needs retail is the thinnest category: 1.2% of mapped places against 2.5% in Bengaluru. Only 13 supermarket-chain outlets are mapped (DMart 1, Reliance Smart/Fresh 3, Vishal Mega Mart 6, Big Bazaar 2, Spencer's 1).
grocery.watch: Neighbourhood kirana stores are the real incumbents and the least completely mapped outlets, so the gap is overstated. Test any site against local store density before acting.

restaurants.read: Restaurants and fast food are 4.7% of mapped places against 7.0%. The big QSR names are present but shallow: Domino's 17 outlets, McDonald's 8, KFC 6 — against 193, 76 and 83 in Bengaluru's core.
restaurants.watch: Independent eateries are numerous and unevenly mapped. Treat the index as a screen; confirm competitor density street by street.

cafes.read: Cafés and tea shops are close to Bengaluru's share (2.3% vs 2.6%), but the specialty and chai chains are missing: no mapped Chaayos, Chai Point, Blue Tokai or Third Wave (22, 50, 15 and 40 in Bengaluru), and Starbucks has 2 outlets (Bengaluru 42).
cafes.watch: Chai stalls dominate and are under-mapped. A café concept here competes on price and habit, not novelty.

desserts.read: Desserts and sweets hold the same 0.8% share as Bengaluru. Baskin Robbins has 7 outlets and Havmor 2; Naturals, Theobroma and Cream Stone have none mapped.
desserts.watch: Traditional sweet shops are the real benchmark here and sit outside most chain lists.

pharmacy.read: Pharmacy and health retail is in line by share (1.3% vs 1.4%), but organised pharmacy is almost absent: 4 Apollo outlets, against 283 Apollo and 273 MedPlus in Bengaluru.
pharmacy.watch: Independent chemists are dense and lightly mapped. Healthcare clusters (Swaroop Nagar, Kalyanpur) are the natural anchors.

fitness.read: Fitness and wellness is in line with Bengaluru's share (4.0% vs 3.8%).
fitness.watch: Gym listings change often and are inconsistently categorised; verify before drawing conclusions.

apparel.read: Apparel, footwear and jewellery is the strongest retail format (6.1% of mapped places vs 5.1%), and value-first chains are already organised: V-Mart has 10 outlets (Bengaluru 10), Raymond 16 (78), Bata 16 (130), Reliance Trends 10 (146). Zudio, Max Fashion and Shoppers Stop have no mapped outlet.
apparel.watch: A crowded, trusted bazaar economy sits behind these numbers. New entrants compete with established multi-brand traders.

banking.read: Banks and finance are 9.9% of mapped places against 6.6% — a trading city's footprint.
banking.watch: This category includes insurance and agency offices, so it overstates branch banking. Use it as a signal of commercial activity, not a bank-branch count.

coaching.read: Coaching is Kanpur's signature: 3.9% of mapped places against 2.4%. Kakadeo–Geeta Nagar (79 centres) and Kidwai Nagar–Yashoda Nagar (54) are the belts.
coaching.watch: Coaching demand is seasonal and exam-cycle driven. Formats that depend on it should be tested across the academic year.
